run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-101 had issues on November 23, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The app-101 payment-api service logged a burst of database-connection-pool errors between 13:46:00Z and 14:44:00Z on 2026-11-23, on the log stream service=payment-api, pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-lpmpl, file /var/log/payment-api.log. Eight ERROR lines carry the exact message 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted', with acquisition wait_time_ms climbing from 1227 to 4840 and queue_length between 5 and 15, while INFO 'Payment processed successfully' lines still appear at 12:57, 13:42 and 13:59 UTC, so the failure was intermittent and payment-api was not down. The observed deviation starts at 13:46:00Z, one minute after the reported 13:45 UTC onset. Loki returned logs only for this payment-api service (no other namespace stream either), and Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable on every attempt, so no other workload can be named as affected and no metric or span evidence exists for the pool, the service or its dependency. The mechanism is confirmed as saturation of payment-api's own connection pool; whether the underlying trigger was a slow or unavailable database or pool sizing/leak inside payment-api remains a hypothesis, so no root-cause object is named. Two candidates were checked and rejected: the otel-demo flagd paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable faults (defaultVariant 'off', and scoped to the demo 'payment' service) and the app-101 Deployment payment-api-101 create/kill activity at 18:40:18-18:40:30Z, roughly five hours after the errors.

claims.text: payment-api in namespace app-101 (stream labels service=payment-api, job=payment-api, pod=payment-api-101-8486559b69-lpmpl, filename /var/log/payment-api.log) logged 8 ERROR lines reading 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' at 13:46:00Z (wait_time_ms 1227, queue_length 10), 13:54:00Z (2104, 11), 14:03:00Z (1495, 8), 14:15:00Z (2965, 9), 14:19:00Z (4005, 10), 14:21:00Z (4840, 8), 14:31:00Z (2358, 15) and 14:44:00Z (3836, 5).

In the 13:45:00Z-13:50:00Z window the earliest line returned is the ERROR timestamped 2026-11-23T13:46:00Z with wait_time_ms 1227 and queue_length 10, so the observed deviation begins one minute after the reported 13:45 UTC start.

Acquisition wait in those error lines grew from wait_time_ms 1227 at 13:46:00Z to 4840 at 14:21:00Z while queue_length stayed between 5 and 15, which is the connection-acquisition wait the messages report for the exhausted pool.
payment-api continued to complete payments around the burst: INFO 'Payment processed successfully' with payment_id PAY-1813 at 12:57:00Z, PAY-5032 at 13:42:00Z and PAY-1800 at 13:59:00Z.

The 13:45:00Z-14:45:00Z app-101 log result contained 9 lines from a single stream, service=payment-api: the 8 pool-exhausted ERROR lines plus one INFO success line at 13:59:00Z; no other service's lines appear in that namespace for the incident hour.

The only log line returned across all Loki namespaces for 13:46:00Z-13:47:00Z is that app-101 payment-api ERROR line, so no other application wrote to the available Loki store at the moment the deviation started.

At query time app-101 contains only the loki Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod (loki-66445c6d6f-qpkcz, image grafana/loki:2.9.0, restartCount 0, Ready True) and no payment-api Deployment, ReplicaSet or Pod; the cluster-wide pod listing shows no payment-api pod in any namespace.

A Deployment named payment-api-101 does exist in app-101: at 18:40:18Z it emitted ScalingReplicaSet (replica set payment-api-101-8486559b69 scaled from 0 to 1), the ReplicaSet emitted SuccessfulCreate for pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-lpmpl, containers python:3.9-slim and grafana/promtail:2.9.0 were Created and Started at 18:40:19-18:40:20Z, and both were killed at 18:40:30Z - about five hours after the 13:46-14:44 error burst.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap defines payment-named fault flags 'paymentFailure' (variants 100%:1, 90%:0.95, 75%:0.75, 50%:0.5, 25%:0.25, 10%:0.1, off:0) and 'paymentUnreachable' (variants on:true, off:false), both state ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off'.

The only database object visible is app-223 sqlserver (Deployment/ReplicaSet sqlserver-78f67c549b, image mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest): its Service was created at 18:42:50Z and its Endpoints contain only a notReadyAddress for pod sqlserver-78f67c549b-b6gkp, all after the incident window.

The failed connection acquisitions trace to payment-api's downstream database becoming slow or unavailable: every error names database-connection acquisition, wait rose to 4840 ms with up to 15 queued waiters, yet charges still completed. No database telemetry (logs, metrics, spans) was retrievable, so this dependency-side cause is unverified.

An alternative candidate is a pool sizing or connection-leak defect inside payment-api (max pool size, acquire timeout, max lifetime), which would emit the same 'pool exhausted' message with no database fault. payment-api's Deployment spec and any pool-config ConfigMap are absent from the queried cluster, so this remains unchecked.

The otel-demo flagd faults 'paymentFailure' and 'paymentUnreachable' are not the cause of the app-101 payment-api errors: both are set to defaultVariant 'off' in the value read, they target the otel-demo 'payment' demo service rather than the app-101 payment-api workload, and the observed app-101 messages are database-connection failures, not charge failures injected by flagd.

The app-101 Deployment payment-api-101 scale-up at 18:40:18Z and the kill of pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-lpmpl at 18:40:30Z did not cause the 13:45 UTC incident: they occur roughly five hours after the 13:46-14:44 error burst, that pod ran a promtail:2.9.0 sidecar plus a python:3.9-slim container, and it does not appear in the 13:45-14:45 log result.

Collect database-side evidence for the payment-api dependency (reachability, connection count, blocking/slow queries, restarts) over 2026-11-23 13:40-14:50 UTC, and compare it with payment-api's max pool size and acquire timeout, since the logged wait_time_ms and queue_length describe the pool rather than the database itself.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger reachability so payment-api error rate and latency can be measured against a pre-13:45 baseline, and add pool-saturation alerting on connection-acquire wait and queue length rather than relying on application ERROR lines alone.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable on every attempt (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no payment-api or database error-rate, latency or pool metric series were read and no latency baseline exists.

Jaeger was unavailable on every attempt (traces_search and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no payment-api spans exist and no parent-child edge to a database can be confirmed or denied.

Loki holds only payment-api streams: queries for app-223 over 13:40-14:00Z (81fc96f3-9118-4951-9760-3eb027939d3b-t1:d3588476-dc69-4f4b-ba46-1788b9622b17) and 13:00-14:30Z (d0d510f6-110b-410d-ad00-c61c05241384-t1:a8cc4424-1e4c-4a3e-9011-0891aa8f7293) returned no lines, so the database side is unobservable and no other service can be named as affected or cleared on log evidence.

Loki queries for app-101 ERROR lines at 11:00-13:45Z (81fc96f3-9118-4951-9760-3eb027939d3b-t0:a29f4920-f7cb-4266-ba60-661bf10dc930), 14:45-17:00Z (ca1d7191-8ab2-4c30-8c8c-e6a3c6db2fa2-t0:c88431d3-5350-48ff-902f-c6164e2194c7) and 17:00-18:41Z (165312a7-d8f7-4b07-b2e0-0ee520b9176d-t0:63a64e61-9057-4bfc-be8a-db6ca1f37ec8), and for 2026-11-22 13:00-14:00Z (ca1d7191-8ab2-4c30-8c8c-e6a3c6db2fa2-t1:7060e351-a89d-486e-902c-9439d7e900c1), all returned no_data, so it is not established whether these errors existed before 13:46 or after 14:44 or are first-time.

fetch_pod_logs for pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-lpmpl in namespace otel-demo returned no_data with no previous container instance, and Loki's all-namespace query for 13:45-13:50Z other than app-101 returned no_data (1edd68e4-24ac-4b32-870c-d5d6dbb6968c-t0:9d260609-f11d-4fd7-8c4b-103af7632154), so the identity and namespace mapping of the logging pod could only be taken from the Loki labels.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so what changed at or just before 13:45 UTC (deployment, config or database) is unknown.

payment-api's Deployment spec, pool configuration and ConfigMap are not present in the queried cluster (app-101 holds only loki-config and promtail-config ConfigMaps; no payment-api Pod/Deployment object exists), so pool size, database host and timeout settings could not be read.

Kubernetes objects were readable only in their post-incident state; the payment-api pod that produced the 13:46-14:44 logs is absent, so its status, restart count, last termination reason and incident-window events are unknown.

Kubernetes churn at 18:27-18:40Z (app-101 loki rollout, app-101 payment-api-101 scale-up then kill, app-223 sqlserver ReplicaSet created 18:42:50Z) happened hours after the incident; the actor and reason for that churn are not recorded in the evidence, so it is recorded as a gap rather than as impact.
next_steps: Obtain database-side telemetry (slow-query log, connection counts, blocking, restarts) for the payment-api dependency covering 2026-11-23 13:40-14:50 UTC to test or refute the downstream-database hypothesis.
Retrieve the payment-api deployment manifest and pool settings (max pool size, acquire timeout, max lifetime) to test the pool-sizing or leak hypothesis.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access and re-run payment-api error-rate and latency queries against a pre-13:45 baseline, plus queries for any database exporter series.
Pull change history for 2026-11-23 13:00-14:00 UTC once the change_history integration is available.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.prometheus.yml:
global:
  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s
storage:
  tsdb:
    out_of_order_time_window: 30m
otlp:
    keep_identifying_resource_attributes: true
    promote_resource_attributes:
    - opspilot.integration.id
    - service.instance.id
    - service.name
    - service.namespace
    - service.version
    - cloud.availability_zone
    - cloud.region
    - deployment.environment.name
    - k8s.cluster.name
    - k8s.container.name
    - k8s.cronjob.name
    - k8s.daemonset.name
    - k8s.deployment.name
    - k8s.job.name
    - k8s.namespace.name
    - k8s.node.name
    - k8s.pod.name
    - k8s.replicaset.name
    - k8s.statefulset.name
    - container.name
    - host.name
rule_files:
- /etc/config/recording_rules.yml
- /etc/config/alerting_rules.yml
- /etc/config/rules
- /etc/config/alerts
scrape_configs:

  static_configs:
  - targets:
    - localhost:9090
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-apiservers
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  relabel_configs:

    regex: default;kubernetes;https
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    - __meta_kubernetes_endpoint_port_name
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-nodes
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node
  relabel_configs:
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)
  - replacement: kubernetes.default.svc:443
    target_label: __address__
  - regex: (.+)
    replacement: /api/v1/nodes/$1/proxy/metrics
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_node_name
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-nodes-cadvisor
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node
  relabel_configs:
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: A line that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only limit lines are shown (the newest), and retention, ingest delay, the label selector and line filters can leave gaps. The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | select(.metadata.namespace != "otel-demo") | {ns: .metadata.namespace, name: .metadata.name, keys: (.data|keys)}

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
